subject: A free share of SpaceX, and who pays for it
summary: SpaceX and Musk promise shares to children with Trump Accounts, a wrestler dies, and Reuters reports a breach of an Air Force cloud.

lead.head: The gift is a share, and the share is a pitch
text: Giving every child with a Trump Account a share of SpaceX is a marketing move dressed as generosity. That is my read, and the record is plain about what happened. The company says it will give one share to each child with an active account. Musk says he will add a second.

It follows a pledge he made in October, so this is a promise being widened, not a new idea. A later post from Musk says he will give another share every year. The paper has not checked that one. Promises like this cost little on the day they are made. The bill arrives later, when somebody has to deliver the shares and say who owns them.

notes.head: WWE reports a death and says little
notes.text: WWE says the wrestler Bronson Reed has died. It cited medical complications and gave no more. He was reported hurt at an event three weeks earlier, and WWE has not linked the two. Until it does, the two facts sit side by side and nothing connects them.

notes.head: A breach story that rests on anonymous sources
notes.text: Reuters reports that hackers breached the Air Force's Cloud One platform. Its sources say the intrusion touches air defense, munitions tracking and personnel systems. The Air Force has not confirmed it. The story carries real weight if it holds, and it has only one outlet's sourcing so far.

notes.head: Two men killed, two descriptions
notes.text: MSF says two of its watchmen died in a direct hit on a marked clinic in Gaza. The Israeli military says it killed two Hamas members who worked as guards there. Both accounts name the same two dead men and describe different people. Nothing in the record settles which is right.

text: Friday was a day of claims that outran their proof. A pledge with no delivery date, a breach with no confirmation, a strike with two identities for the dead.
My call is to wait for the second source on each. The SpaceX promise is the easiest to test, because shares either arrive or they do not.
